issue_context.title: State of switch pi4ioe5v9xxxx not equal to hardware state on startup if inverted
issue_context.body:
## The problem
In the configuration file the parameter "invert_logic" can be set true. If that is the case, on startup the switches in the GUI will be switched off, but the hardware will be in 'on' state as the  pi4ioe5v9xxxx chips are initialized in 0-state. Code should be added to explicit initialize the hardware on startup.


## Environment


- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117.0.dev0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): -
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core):  RPi
- Integration causing this issue:  pi4ioe5v9xxxx
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/pi4ioe5v9xxxx/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```yaml
switch:
  - platform: pi4ioe5v9xxxx
    i2c_bus: 1
    invert_logic: True
    pins:
      01: MainRelay 230V
```

review_comments: We usually don't actuate changes when adding the entity. Why should we do that?
Can't we just set the state of the entity to the state of the device?

No, the hardware is write-only if configured as output. What actually happens is the following:
- Hardware I was running is a rpi with I2C connection to these driver chips
- Hardware is started from off to on (power up)
- HA is starting up. All switche-states are off, as they do not remember their state. 
- If the 'inverse' bit for a switch is set, the switch-state 'off' means: hardware should be 'on'
- As the driver chips is in its default startup condition (off), this is not the case. 
- What is more confusing: the state in the inteface shown is the software state, so the state in the interface is 'off', while in hardware it is 'on'.

This should fix that. 

For restarts of HA-software only, saving the state could also fix this, but that does not fix the power-reboot-issue.

Yeah, my suggestion is to simply change the internal entity state to match the current hardware state without changing the hardware state.

How do we know that the user wants the hardware to turn off when we restart home assistant?
